chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Tell me, a rider stopping on the way, if he is not in a state of wudu (ablution), what should he do when he is unable to dismount? He said: He should perform tayammum from the felt cloth, or his saddle, or the mane of his riding animal, for there is dust in them, and he should pray.

key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: performed dry ablution in place of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.غُبَارًا: dust, which serves as the material for tayammum
key_terms.لِبْدِهِ: the felt cloth or pad associated with the saddle
key_terms.مَعْرِفَةِ دَابَّتِهِ: the mane of his riding animal

ai.seo_question: How should a person perform tayammum if they cannot get down from their mount and do not have wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who cannot dismount and lacks wudu (ablution). Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام instructs that tayammum may be performed using dust found on riding equipment or the animal’s mane, after which one may perform salat (prayer).
